inhumane.oewn-01265721-a.label: negative
inhumane.oewn-01265721-a.tone: The institutional word - it is conditions, treatment and policies that get called inhumane.

barbarous.oewn-01266123-s.label: negative
barbarous.oewn-01266123-s.tone: Condemns as a whole civilisation would: this is beneath what people owe each other.

brutal.oewn-01266123-s.label: negative
brutal.oewn-01266123-s.tone: Plain and physical. The commonest of the strong words, and the least ornamented.

cruel.oewn-01266123-s.label: negative
cruel.oewn-01266123-s.tone: The central moral charge: the suffering was known about and inflicted anyway.

fell.oewn-01266123-s.label: negative
fell.oewn-01266123-s.tone: Survives almost only in *one fell swoop*; on its own it reads as deliberate archaism.

roughshod.oewn-01266123-s.label: negative
roughshod.oewn-01266123-s.tone: Only ever *ride roughshod over*, and it is about disregard rather than violence.

savage.oewn-01266123-s.label: negative
savage.oewn-01266123-s.tone: Carries a colonial history of describing whole peoples; strongest when kept for acts.

vicious.oewn-01266123-s.label: negative
vicious.oewn-01266123-s.tone: Adds enjoyment to the harm - a vicious act is one the doer wanted to do.

beastly.oewn-01266555-s.label: negative
beastly.oewn-01266555-s.tone: British and largely trivial now (*beastly weather*); the cruelty has drained out of it.

bestial.oewn-01266555-s.label: negative
bestial.oewn-01266555-s.tone: Denies the person's humanity outright, which is why it is reserved for atrocity.

brute.oewn-01266555-s.label: negative
brute.oewn-01266555-s.tone: Mostly attributive - *brute force* is unreasoning rather than wicked.

brutish.oewn-01266555-s.label: negative
brutish.oewn-01266555-s.tone: Coarse rather than violent: it says unrefined more than it says cruel.

cannibalic.oewn-01266942-s.label: negative
cannibalic.oewn-01266942-s.tone: The furthest word in the family, and rare enough to sound like an accusation of myth.

cold.oewn-01267081-s.label: negative
cold.oewn-01267081-s.tone: The absence of feeling, not its violence. A cold refusal need never raise its voice.

cold-blooded.oewn-01267081-s.label: negative
cold-blooded.oewn-01267081-s.tone: Premeditation is the whole charge - the harm was planned while calm.

inhuman.oewn-01267081-s.label: negative
inhuman.oewn-01267081-s.tone: Names what is missing rather than what was done; harsher than *inhumane*, which describes conditions.

kind.oewn-01374976-a.label: positive
kind.oewn-01374976-a.tone: The plain, unshowy word, and the one people most want said about them.

benignant.oewn-01375495-s.label: positive
benignant.oewn-01375495-s.tone: Literary and top-down - warmth extended by someone with the power not to bother.

gracious.oewn-01375495-s.label: positive
gracious.oewn-01375495-s.tone: Courtesy from a position of advantage; graciousness costs the giver nothing.

benign.oewn-01375700-s.label: positive
benign.oewn-01375700-s.tone: Weakened by medicine, where a benign growth is merely not malignant.

charitable.oewn-01375875-s.label: positive
charitable.oewn-01375875-s.tone: Splits in two: charitable giving is warm, a *charitable interpretation* is faintly condescending.

benevolent.oewn-01375875-s.label: positive
benevolent.oewn-01375875-s.tone: Formal and settled - a disposition rather than a mood, which is why institutions claim it.

kindly.oewn-01375875-s.label: positive
kindly.oewn-01375875-s.tone: Softer and older than *kind*, and now used mostly of the elderly.

sympathetic.oewn-01375875-s.label: positive
sympathetic.oewn-01375875-s.tone: Kindness aimed at someone in difficulty; it presumes there is trouble to meet.

good-hearted.oewn-01375875-s.label: positive
good-hearted.oewn-01375875-s.tone: Locates the kindness in the character, and forgives clumsiness in carrying it out.

openhearted.oewn-01375875-s.label: positive
openhearted.oewn-01375875-s.tone: Kindness without self-protection - the giver is not holding anything back.

large-hearted.oewn-01375875-s.label: positive
large-hearted.oewn-01375875-s.tone: Capacity, not just intent: there is room in this person for more than their own concerns.

gentle.oewn-01376241-s.label: positive
gentle.oewn-01376241-s.tone: Kindness expressed as restraint - the force that was available was not used.

kindhearted.oewn-01376472-s.label: positive
kindhearted.oewn-01376472-s.tone: Innate rather than practised; the kindness precedes the occasion for it.

kind-hearted.oewn-01376472-s.label: positive
kind-hearted.oewn-01376472-s.tone: The hyphenated spelling of the same word, equally warm.

gluttonous.oewn-00009997-a.label: negative
gluttonous.oewn-00009997-a.tone: Names one of the seven deadly sins; the excess is a moral failure, not an appetite.

crapulous.oewn-00010404-s.label: negative
crapulous.oewn-00010404-s.tone: Formal and disgusted, and about drink as much as food.

crapulent.oewn-00010556-s.label: negative
crapulent.oewn-00010556-s.tone: Describes the sick aftermath rather than the appetite - more pitiable than blamed.

edacious.oewn-00010745-s.label: negative
edacious.oewn-00010745-s.tone: Rare enough to sound playful; almost nobody is called this in earnest.

esurient.oewn-00010745-s.label: negative
esurient.oewn-00010745-s.tone: Literary and dry, and often used of curiosity rather than food.

rapacious.oewn-00010745-s.label: negative
rapacious.oewn-00010745-s.tone: Has left the table entirely - it is now said of companies and landlords who take what they can.

ravening.oewn-00010745-s.label: negative
ravening.oewn-00010745-s.tone: Predatory and archaic-sounding, as of a beast that has not eaten.

ravenous.oewn-00010745-s.label: negative
ravenous.oewn-00010745-s.tone: Usually just very hungry, and often said cheerfully of oneself.

voracious.oewn-00010745-s.label: negative
voracious.oewn-00010745-s.tone: Frequently admiring - a *voracious reader* is being praised, not scolded.

wolfish.oewn-00010745-s.label: negative
wolfish.oewn-00010745-s.tone: Adds hunger to the manner of eating; it watches the food the way a predator would.

greedy.oewn-00011179-s.label: negative
greedy.oewn-00011179-s.tone: The everyday charge, and one of the first moral words a child is taught.

hoggish.oewn-00011346-s.label: negative
hoggish.oewn-00011346-s.tone: Compares the eater to a pig outright, with none of the softening *piggy* has.

piggish.oewn-00011346-s.label: negative
piggish.oewn-00011346-s.tone: The same comparison, and the commoner of the two insults.

piggy.oewn-00011346-s.label: negative
piggy.oewn-00011346-s.tone: Diminutive enough to be used of children without real anger.

porcine.oewn-00011346-s.label: negative
porcine.oewn-00011346-s.tone: Formal, and usually about shape rather than appetite - which makes it a colder insult.

swinish.oewn-00011346-s.label: negative
swinish.oewn-00011346-s.tone: Broader than eating: it condemns the whole manner of the person.

stingy.oewn-01116284-a.label: negative
stingy.oewn-01116284-a.tone: The plain word. Its mirror image is *thrifty*, which praises the identical behaviour.

ungenerous.oewn-01116284-a.label: negative
ungenerous.oewn-01116284-a.tone: Names the missing virtue rather than the present vice, which makes it the politer complaint.

beggarly.oewn-01116711-s.label: negative
beggarly.oewn-01116711-s.tone: Said of the sum, not the person - an amount so small it insults whoever receives it.

mean.oewn-01116711-s.label: negative
mean.oewn-01116711-s.tone: In British use this is the standard word for stingy; American readers hear *cruel* instead.

cheap.oewn-01116856-s.label: negative
cheap.oewn-01116856-s.tone: The gloss is *embarrassingly stingy* - the shame is the point, and it is public.

chintzy.oewn-01116856-s.label: negative
chintzy.oewn-01116856-s.tone: Slides between stingy and shoddy; either way it is a sneer at what was provided.

cheeseparing.oewn-01116967-s.label: negative
cheeseparing.oewn-01116967-s.tone: Formal and disdainful, usually aimed at budgets rather than people.

close.oewn-01116967-s.label: negative
close.oewn-01116967-s.tone: Euphemistic. *Close with money* is what you say when you do not want to say stingy.

near.oewn-01116967-s.label: negative
near.oewn-01116967-s.tone: The same euphemism, now dated and chiefly British.

penny-pinching.oewn-01116967-s.label: negative
penny-pinching.oewn-01116967-s.tone: Pictures the act, and the smallness of the coin does the condemning.

skinny.oewn-01116967-s.label: negative
skinny.oewn-01116967-s.tone: This sense is rare and easily missed - a reader will hear the body word first.

closefisted.oewn-01117247-s.label: negative
closefisted.oewn-01117247-s.tone: The hand that will not open; the oldest image in the family.

hardfisted.oewn-01117247-s.label: negative
hardfisted.oewn-01117247-s.tone: Harder than *closefisted* by a shade, and rarer.

tightfisted.oewn-01117247-s.label: negative
tightfisted.oewn-01117247-s.tone: The commonest of the three fists, and the most vivid.

grudging.oewn-01117378-s.label: negative
grudging.oewn-01117378-s.tone: The money was given - resentfully, which is what makes it worse than refusal for some.

selfish.oewn-02105605-a.label: negative
selfish.oewn-02105605-a.tone: The plain moral word, and the one that gets used in real arguments.

egoistic.oewn-02105605-a.label: negative
egoistic.oewn-02105605-a.tone: Philosophical in origin; it names a doctrine as much as a habit.

egoistical.oewn-02105605-a.label: negative
egoistical.oewn-02105605-a.tone: The same word with an extra syllable, and no extra force.

egocentric.oewn-02105605-a.label: negative
egocentric.oewn-02105605-a.tone: Borrowed from developmental psychology, where it describes children without blaming them.

self-centered.oewn-02105605-a.label: negative
self-centered.oewn-02105605-a.tone: Softer than *selfish* - it describes where attention sits rather than what was taken.

self-centred.oewn-02105605-a.label: negative
self-centred.oewn-02105605-a.tone: The British spelling, identical in force.

self-serving.oewn-02105605-a.label: negative
self-serving.oewn-02105605-a.tone: Adds calculation: the generous-looking act had a private purpose.

self-seeking.oewn-02105605-a.label: negative
self-seeking.oewn-02105605-a.tone: The same charge, aimed at a career rather than a single act.

egotistic.oewn-02105974-s.label: negative
egotistic.oewn-02105974-s.tone: Vanity rather than greed - about talking of oneself, not taking for oneself.

egotistical.oewn-02105974-s.label: negative
egotistical.oewn-02105974-s.tone: The commoner spelling, and a staple of ordinary complaint.

narcissistic.oewn-02105974-s.label: negative
narcissistic.oewn-02105974-s.tone: A clinical diagnosis used as an insult, which is what makes it land so hard.

self-loving.oewn-02105974-s.label: negative
self-loving.oewn-02105974-s.tone: The literal compound, and neutral enough to be reclaimed as self-care.

self-absorbed.oewn-00102878-s.label: negative
self-absorbed.oewn-00102878-s.tone: Inattentive rather than grasping; the harm is what gets overlooked.

self-involved.oewn-00102878-s.label: negative
self-involved.oewn-00102878-s.tone: The same forgivable fault, and the milder of the two phrasings.

humble.oewn-01899020-a.label: positive
humble.oewn-01899020-a.tone: Praise when chosen, plain description when not - *humble origins* passes no judgement.

broken.oewn-01899370-s.label: negative
broken.oewn-01899370-s.tone: Not modesty at all: something was done to this person and it worked.

crushed.oewn-01899370-s.label: negative
crushed.oewn-01899370-s.tone: The heaviest word here, and always about defeat rather than character.

humbled.oewn-01899370-s.label: negative
humbled.oewn-01899370-s.tone: Ambiguous by design. It can mean genuinely moved, or beaten and admitting it.

humiliated.oewn-01899370-s.label: negative
humiliated.oewn-01899370-s.tone: Requires an audience - the lowering had to be seen to count.

low.oewn-01899370-s.label: negative
low.oewn-01899370-s.tone: Status, not disposition; the older sense that *humble origins* still carries.

meek.oewn-01899577-s.label: neutral
meek.oewn-01899577-s.tone: Praised in the Beatitudes and faintly disparaged everywhere else since.

mild.oewn-01899577-s.label: positive
mild.oewn-01899577-s.tone: Gentleness of manner with no claim about the will behind it.

modest.oewn-01899577-s.label: positive
modest.oewn-01899577-s.tone: The virtue the family is named for: an accurate view of oneself, held without fuss.

uncivil.oewn-00645747-a.label: negative
uncivil.oewn-00645747-a.tone: Formal and slightly distant - the complaint of someone invoking a standard.

rude.oewn-00645747-a.label: negative
rude.oewn-00645747-a.tone: The everyday word, learned early, and blunt enough to be used to a child's face.

dirty.oewn-00420808-a.label: negative
dirty.oewn-00420808-a.tone: The plain word, and the one that carries a second, moral life (*a dirty trick*).

soiled.oewn-00420808-a.label: negative
soiled.oewn-00420808-a.tone: Clinical and euphemistic - the word hospitals and laundries use to avoid *dirty*.

unclean.oewn-00420808-a.label: negative
unclean.oewn-00420808-a.tone: Religious in origin; it condemns the thing as unfit rather than merely dirty.

bedraggled.oewn-00421806-s.label: negative
bedraggled.oewn-00421806-s.tone: Pitiable rather than blamed - the rain did this, not the person.

draggled.oewn-00421806-s.label: negative
draggled.oewn-00421806-s.tone: The older and rarer half of *bedraggled*, with the same sympathy.

befouled.oewn-00421999-s.label: negative
befouled.oewn-00421999-s.tone: Formal and disgusted, and it implies an agent: someone fouled this.

fouled.oewn-00421999-s.label: negative
fouled.oewn-00421999-s.tone: The plainer form, common in reports about water and air.

begrimed.oewn-00422169-s.label: negative
begrimed.oewn-00422169-s.tone: Dirt from work, and often faintly admiring of the labour that caused it.

dingy.oewn-00422169-s.label: negative
dingy.oewn-00422169-s.tone: Said of rooms and fabric, and the real complaint is that it is depressing.

grimy.oewn-00422169-s.label: negative
grimy.oewn-00422169-s.tone: Descriptive and physical; grime is a fact about a surface, not a fault.

grubby.oewn-00422169-s.label: negative
grubby.oewn-00422169-s.tone: Mild enough to be affectionate about a child, and mildly damning about a motive.

grungy.oewn-00422169-s.label: negative
grungy.oewn-00422169-s.tone: Informal and unimpressed, though a whole music scene wore it as a badge.

raunchy.oewn-00422169-s.label: negative
raunchy.oewn-00422169-s.tone: This dirt sense is dated; a modern reader will hear the sexual one first.

black.oewn-00422521-s.label: negative
black.oewn-00422521-s.tone: Literal soot in this sense, and one of a great many senses this word carries.

smutty.oewn-00422521-s.label: negative
smutty.oewn-00422521-s.tone: The soot sense has been almost entirely displaced by the obscene one.

buggy.oewn-00422721-s.label: negative
buggy.oewn-00422721-s.tone: Infested rather than soiled, which most readers find the worse of the two.

cheerful.oewn-00363547-a.label: positive
cheerful.oewn-00363547-a.tone: The steady everyday word - a disposition rather than a burst of feeling.

beaming.oewn-00363972-s.label: positive
beaming.oewn-00363972-s.tone: The cheer has reached the face and is impossible to miss.

glad.oewn-00363972-s.label: positive
glad.oewn-00363972-s.tone: Older and quieter than *happy*, and it usually points at a reason.

beamish.oewn-00364111-s.label: positive
beamish.oewn-00364111-s.tone: Kept alive almost entirely by *Jabberwocky*; it sounds invented, because it nearly is.

smiling.oewn-00364111-s.label: positive
smiling.oewn-00364111-s.tone: Describes the evidence rather than the mood, which is why it can be worn falsely.

twinkly.oewn-00364111-s.label: positive
twinkly.oewn-00364111-s.tone: Warm but faintly patronising - it is mostly said of older people's eyes.

blithe.oewn-00364371-s.label: positive
blithe.oewn-00364371-s.tone: Splits sharply: blithe spirits are charming, *blithe disregard* is careless.

blithesome.oewn-00364371-s.label: positive
blithesome.oewn-00364371-s.tone: The archaic-sounding form, and used now only when the writer wants that flavour.

lighthearted.oewn-00364371-s.label: positive
lighthearted.oewn-00364371-s.tone: Free of weight rather than full of joy - the burden is what is missing.

lightsome.oewn-00364371-s.label: positive
lightsome.oewn-00364371-s.tone: Rare, and pulled between light-of-heart and light-of-foot.

light-hearted.oewn-00364371-s.label: positive
light-hearted.oewn-00364371-s.tone: The hyphenated spelling, equally common and equally warm.

buoyant.oewn-00364701-s.label: positive
buoyant.oewn-00364701-s.tone: Cheer that resists being pushed down; the metaphor is a thing that will not sink.

chirpy.oewn-00364701-s.label: positive
chirpy.oewn-00364701-s.tone: British and small-scale, and grating if the hearer is not cheerful too.

perky.oewn-00364701-s.label: positive
perky.oewn-00364701-s.tone: Brisk and a little relentless - it can condescend when said of an adult.

cheery.oewn-00365018-s.label: positive
cheery.oewn-00365018-s.tone: Outward-facing: a cheery greeting is aimed at somebody.

gay.oewn-00365018-s.label: positive
gay.oewn-00365018-s.tone: This bright-and-pleasant sense is now thoroughly dated; the modern sense has replaced it.

loyal.oewn-00964581-a.label: positive
loyal.oewn-00964581-a.tone: The plain word and the strongest, because it needs no institution to make sense.

allegiant.oewn-00964856-s.label: positive
allegiant.oewn-00964856-s.tone: Formal and rare - it names the duty rather than the feeling.

doglike.oewn-00965097-s.label: positive
doglike.oewn-00965097-s.tone: Devotion with the dignity taken out; praise and belittlement in the same word.

hard-core.oewn-00965214-s.label: positive
hard-core.oewn-00965214-s.tone: Intensity without direction, which is why it attaches as easily to extremists as to fans.

hardcore.oewn-00965214-s.label: positive
hardcore.oewn-00965214-s.tone: The unhyphenated spelling, commoner now than the hyphen.

leal.oewn-00965324-s.label: positive
leal.oewn-00965324-s.tone: Scottish and archaic, kept alive by *the land o' the leal*.

liege.oewn-00965495-s.label: positive
liege.oewn-00965495-s.tone: Feudal and historical: allegiance owed by rank, not chosen.

true-blue.oewn-00965665-s.label: positive
true-blue.oewn-00965665-s.tone: Loyalty proved over time, and in Britain it also means Conservative.
